forecasts.rationale: The ECB raised the deposit rate to 2.50% on Sept 10. Rates futures had about a 60% chance of an October hike on Sept 24, so a hike stays a real risk.

Base rate for ECB meetings is roughly a 60% chance of no change given recent tightening cycles, but the September 25bp hike and hawkish comments shift odds toward another increase. Market futures priced a 60% chance of an October hike, while analyst views are split (Danske expects a hike, Goldman/UBS see December, MUFG sees no further hikes), implying about a one‑third chance of an October hike from that perspective. Averaging the market and analyst signals yields ~46‑47% probability of a hike, so the probability of no change is about 55%.

The base rate for no change at a meeting following a recent hike is moderate, but Lagarde's unexpectedly dovish early-October comments, emphasizing that rising long-term yields will slow growth and damp inflation pass-through, significantly reduce the likelihood of a hike. Ebury's judgment that an October hike is unlikely and the shift from prior futures pricing (60% hike probability before the dovish tone) support a higher chance of no change, though lingering hawkish risks from September's inflation beat and Nagel's cautious stance prevent a higher probability.

The base rate favors a pause after a September hike, and Lagarde's early-October dovish pivot—arguing that higher long-term yields will slow growth and dampen energy pass-through—combined with Ebury's assessment that an October hike is unlikely, strongly point to no change. While futures had priced a significant chance of a hike as of late September and some analysts still expect one, the freshest guidance from the ECB President tilts the balance toward steady rates. The main risks to this view are a further upside inflation surprise or an escalation in the Iran war before the meeting.

The base rate for a hold in an active hiking cycle is roughly 50-60%, but the September 25bp hike and inflation beat made another increase plausible. The main evidence shifting the estimate is Lagarde's early-October dovish tone and Ebury's view that an October hike is unlikely, which favors a hold. A surprise energy shock, stronger inflation data, or hawkish ECB officials could still push the market toward a 25bp increase.

Base rate for ECB holding rates steady at any given meeting is roughly 50-60%. The evidence is mixed: futures priced ~60% for a hike in late September, but Lagarde's early October dovish comments and Ebury's assessment that an October hike is unlikely pull toward no change. Goldman, UBS, and MUFG expect no October hike, while Danske expects one. The dovish shift in Lagarde's tone and the tightening of financial conditions via higher long-term yields suggest the ECB will likely pause in October, though a September inflation beat keeps the possibility of a hike alive.

questions.question: Will the ECB announce no change at the October 2026 meeting?
questions.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the change in basis points in the deposit facility rate resulting from the October 2026 meeting of the European Central Bank, relative to the level it was prior to this meeting.

The resolution source will be official information from the European Central Bank, including the statement or release from its October 2026 meeting, scheduled for October 28-29, 2026, as listed on the official European Central Bank calendar (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the European Central Bank's October 2026 meeting with relevant data is issued.

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound.

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of “Increase” or “Decrease” will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size.

If the specified meeting is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed meeting. If the specified meeting is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the “No Change” bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified meeting will not be considered.

forecasts.rationale: Polls split by pollster: CRTA (June) had the Student List at 44.9% against 35.7% for SNS, while government-friendly Faktor Plus (Sept 16-20) had Vucic's United Serbia list at 48.6% to 37.1%. In 2023 SNS polled close to its result. The ruling list keeps strong media and administrative advantages and a consolidated bloc, so the students winning the most seats is plausible but less likely than not.

Base rate strongly favors SNS, which has won every parliamentary election since 2012 with institutional advantages including media control and state resources. The evidence is sharply divided: a reputable CRTA/Stanford face-to-face poll (June, n=2,324) showed the Student List leading 44.9% to 35.7%, but a more recent Faktor Plus poll (Sept) shows SNS ahead 48.6% to 37.1%. The snap election timing (called Sept 8 for Oct 25) disadvantages the nascent student list's organization. While the student movement is unprecedented and could mobilize protest voters, the polling divergence and SNS's structural advantages make the Student List an underdog to win the most seats.

The base rate for an opposition list to win the most seats in Serbian parliamentary elections is low, given the SNS’s consistent dominance since 2012 (historically around 10‑15% chance for a non‑SNS plurality). Recent polling shows mixed signals: an earlier CRTA/Stanford poll had the Student List leading 44.9% to 35.7%, but a more recent Faktor Plus survey (Sept 16‑20) placed the Vucic‑led United Serbia list ahead 48.6% to 37.1%, a margin that translates into a likely seat advantage under Serbia’s electoral system. The ruling party’s control of most national broadcast media further supports its ability to sustain turnout and voter loyalty. While protest momentum could boost the Student List, the weight of the more recent poll and historical trends suggests a modest chance of an upset.

The base rate for an opposition list winning the most seats in Serbia is low, as the ruling SNS has dominated since 2012. The most recent poll (Faktor Plus, Sept 16-20) shows the SNS-led list at 48.6% and the Student List at 37.1%, a significant lead, though an earlier CRTA/Stanford poll (June) had the Student List ahead. Given the incumbency advantage, media control, and the snap election timing suggesting Vucic's confidence, the Student List is the underdog, but the protest movement's momentum and polling volatility keep the probability above zero.

Base rate: The ruling SNS and its allies have won every Serbian parliamentary election since 2012, and incumbents in the region typically benefit from media control and state resources. Evidence: Polls diverge sharply—an independent June face-to-face survey gave the Student List a nine-point lead among committed voters, while a more recent government-leaning mid-September poll placed the Vucic-led list ahead by roughly eleven points, though the student list was gaining ground. What could change it: A heavy state-media campaign and superior turnout machinery could solidify the government's lead, while a surge in youth turnout or undecided voters breaking against the status quo could deliver a plurality to the students.

The base rate favors the incumbent Vucic-led list, and the latest September poll has United Serbia ahead of the Student List by 11.5 points, which would likely translate into the most seats. The main reason not to be more confident is that an earlier face-to-face CRTA/Stanford poll had the Student List ahead, the student protest movement is strong, and Serbia's polling/media environment is noisy. A final surge or turnout shift could still put the Student List first, but the recent poll makes an upset less likely.

Base rate favors the incumbent SNS, which has dominated Serbian elections for years with structural advantages including control of most national broadcast media. Polling evidence is sharply divided: CRTA/Stanford (June) shows Student List leading 44.9% to 35.7%, while the more recent Faktor Plus poll (September) shows SNS/United Serbia leading 48.6% to 37.1%, though the Student List gained 5.6 points recently. The student protest movement has genuine momentum and one credible poll puts it ahead, but the 11.5-point gap in the most recent poll, combined with historical patterns of polls underestimating SNS due to media asymmetry and turnout dynamics, makes a Student List plurality unlikely though not implausible.

forecasts.rationale: Euro area GDP grew 1.2% year on year in Q2 2026 (third estimate, Sept 7), up from 0.6% in Q1, with a strong 0.6% q/q. The energy shock and possible Irish payback point to a weaker Q3, so 0.8-1.0% is about as likely as 1.1% or more (a 1.1% print counts toward the higher bracket). Trading Economics forecasts 1.0%.

The Trading Economics forecast of 1.0% y/y centers in the 0.8-1.1% range, supported by Q2's upward revision to 1.2% y/y and favorable base effects from weak Q3 2025 growth. However, ECB rate hikes in July and September 2026 plus the Iran war energy shock create material downside risk, and the narrow 0.3pp range with three weeks until the flash estimate implies significant uncertainty.

Base rate: historically, Eurozone Q3 YoY GDP growth falls in the 0.8‑1.1% range only about a quarter of the time. Recent evidence shows Q2 2026 YoY growth at +1.2% (up from +0.6% in Q1) and Trading Economics' model forecasts Q3 2026 at +1.0% YoY, suggesting the economy is hovering around the middle of the target band. The ECB's rate hikes and energy‑price shock pose downside risks, while a stronger‑than‑expected rebound from the Iran‑war shock could push growth above 1.1%. Balancing these factors yields a moderate probability that the flash estimate will land between 0.8% and 1.1% (exclusive of 1.1).

The base rate for a narrow GDP growth range is low, but the Trading Economics model forecast of 1.0% y/y for Q3 2026, combined with a low base from Q3 2025, suggests a reasonable chance of the outcome falling in the 0.8-1.0% range (Yes). However, the ECB rate hikes and energy price shock from the Iran war introduce downside risks that could push growth below 0.8% or keep it at 1.0%, making the probability moderately above 50%.

The base rate for Eurozone annual GDP growth landing in any given 0.3 percentage point bracket is roughly 1/3. Recent data shows Q2 2026 at 1.2% y/y (revised up) and Q1 at 0.6% y/y, suggesting momentum but with ECB rate hikes and energy shock weighing on growth. Trading Economics' model forecast of 1.0% y/y for Q3 2026 falls squarely in the 0.8-1.1% bracket, but the wide range of possible outcomes given the energy shock and rate hikes keeps probability below 50%.

Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the initial release of the specified report will not be considered for this market's resolution.

questions.question: 🇺🇸 Will the Fed raise interest rates in October 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria:
Resolve YES if the Federal Open Market Committee increases the target range for the federal funds rate at its October 27–28, 2026 meeting relative to the target range in effect immediately before the meeting.

Resolve NO if the FOMC leaves the target range unchanged or lowers it.

Resolution will be based on the first official Federal Reserve monetary policy statement issued for the October 27–28, 2026 FOMC meeting.

The size of the increase does not matter. Any increase in the target range counts as YES.

Changes to forward guidance, the balance sheet, quantitative tightening, Treasury operations, or any other policy measure do not count unless the target range for the federal funds rate is also increased.

If the September FOMC decision is delayed beyond the market’s scheduled closing time, the market will remain closed to trading but unresolved until the Federal Reserve publishes the official decision, at which point it will resolve based on that decision

Resolution criteria

This market resolves to YES if Google makes its Gemini 4 Argon model publicly available to individual developers or consumers on or before October 14, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT. Otherwise, this market resolves to NO.

To qualify as publicly available, ordinary individual users must be able to obtain access without being individually selected, invited, vetted, or approved by Google. Qualified access pathways include:

Developer Access: Available via Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, or Google Cloud Vertex AI for any registered developer.

Consumer Access: Offered via a generally available consumer subscription (e.g., Google AI Advanced, Google AI Ultra, or a successor tier) on the Gemini web or mobile interface.

Exclusions and Edge Cases:

Access does not qualify if it remains restricted to enterprise customers, select companies, private-preview cohorts, trusted testers, or members of specific closed initiatives such as Google's Fairwind program.

Paid subscriptions or paid API usage qualify as public access, as long as any ordinary user can sign up and pay.

Geographic restrictions will not prevent a YES resolution, provided ordinary individual users in at least one supported region can obtain unvetted access.

The model must be functionally accessible and interactive by the deadline; a mere announcement of a future release date does not suffice.

Background

Google announced its next-generation frontier AI model, Gemini 4 Argon, on September 30, 2026. Engineered for complex reasoning, multi-step software engineering (scoring 77.9% on DeepSWE v1.1), and defensive cybersecurity, the model boasts a massive 1-million-token output capacity.

At launch, Google made Gemini 4 Argon available exclusively to trusted testers and select cybersecurity partners through its vetted Fairwind program. This market tracks whether Google transitions the model from its restricted early-access phase to general public availability for developers or consumers before the October 15, 2026 deadline.
